criteria: A user can request stations for a country using an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code.
The MCP tool returns a bounded list of stations matching the requested country with enough information to identify and select one.
Selecting a station in the ChatGPT MCP Apps UI updates the player and allows audible playback of a compatible HTTPS stream.
Play, Pause and resume remain available for the selected station.
Invalid country input, no results and provider request failure have clear distinct outcomes.
Dynamic station content is rendered safely and network/CSP constraints are documented.
Appropriate automated tests and MCP Inspector checks pass, and actual ChatGPT selection/playback evidence is recorded separately.

objective: Prepare an approved bounded next phase that adds country-based station discovery and selection to the verified playback proof, without implementing before spec approval.

reports.complexity: Medium. The country query and bounded list are straightforward. Selection touches both MCP tool/UI interaction and audio source lifecycle; provider data must be normalized and safely rendered. Dynamic media CSP and the integration baseline require architecture decisions before coding, and host playback across arbitrary station streams cannot be inferred from the DIAL-001 single-origin proof.
evidence: Radio Browser's primary API reference documents exact country-code lookup at /json/stations/bycountrycodeexact/{searchterm}, with a two-letter ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code; advanced search also accepts countrycode.

Radio Browser station list calls accept limit, offset, and hidebroken; documented default limit is 100000, so the integration must specify a small bound. The API asks clients to call /json/url/{stationuuid} on playback for click counting; this behavior has a privacy and failure-path implication that needs a spec decision.

Station metadata and stream URLs are provider-supplied dynamic content. Render labels as text and validate stream URLs as HTTPS. The existing fixed resource CSP permits only one origin, while OpenAI MCP Apps docs require resourceDomains for loaded media/resource origins and connectDomains for API calls.

Discovery can be served from the MCP server (Radio Browser API origin is then a server-side dependency); playback currently occurs directly from the UI iframe. A catalog's arbitrary stream origins create a material CSP design choice: bounded origin allowlist, another supported policy strategy, or a constrained support claim. HTTPS alone does not establish codec compatibility, reachability, or successful playback.

DIAL-001 host rendering and audible Play/Pause/resume were manually confirmed by owner. Its controlled host error-state check remains explicitly waived/deferred; routine DIAL-002 invalid-input, no-result, provider-failure and selected-stream errors are still new required outcomes.
Primary source details and links are recorded in factory/work-items/DIAL-002/evidence/triage-sources.md.
reports.handoff: Prepare PRODUCT.md and TECH.md for review and human approval. Keep scope to country-code discovery, an explicitly bounded station list, selecting one compatible HTTPS stream in the existing player, and clear invalid-input/no-results/provider-failure/playback outcomes. Explicitly decide provider click counting and dynamic stream-origin/CSP handling, state that compatibility evidence applies only to tested origins/streams, define meaningful provider/UI tests plus MCP Inspector checks and separate ChatGPT host playback evidence, and record the DIAL-001/PR #1 integration dependency. Do not implement before the specification is approved and the baseline is resolved.
open_questions: Spec should define the smallest interaction route: likely one user-supplied country code, a bounded list in an MCP tool result, and a selection action that updates the existing player. Decide whether selection happens in the UI via a server tool or via model-directed follow-up calls, and define the user-visible station fields.

Define country-code validation against ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. A two-letter regex alone does not distinguish real codes; choose a maintained/local list or provider validation while preserving distinct invalid-code, no-results, and provider-failure outcomes.
Choose and document a bounded result count, ordering, broken-station policy, and whether pagination is excluded from this proof.

Resolve dynamic media CSP: which origin policy ChatGPT actually accepts for selected catalog streams, and whether scope is limited to a tested/bounded set of compatible HTTPS origins. Do not claim arbitrary Radio Browser streams will play.
Decide whether to call Radio Browser's click-counter endpoint at playback start; account for its provider documentation, IP/play-event disclosure, and separate request-failure behavior.
Foreman should resolve the pending PR #1/default-branch integration dependency before BUILDING. No DIAL-001 waiver reversal is required; preserve the deferred criterion separately.
relevant_code: src/server.ts: one fixed open_radio tool and a single inline MCP Apps resource; its CSP resourceDomains currently contains only the Radio Paradise stream origin.
src/player-controller.ts and src/player.ts: click-driven Play/Pause/retry state on one audio element; the stream source is currently fixed in public/player.html.
test/server.test.js and test/player.test.js: integration/resource/bundle checks and player transition checks; no country provider, station selection, or dynamic stream-origin coverage exists.

factory/work-items/DIAL-002/REQUEST.md and state.json: approval is to prepare the proposal/spec, not implement before spec approval; no name/genre search, favorites, accounts, database, deployment, or background-playback guarantee.

Branch work/DIAL-002 at d49be43 is based on DIAL-001's accepted candidate line. Intake records PR #1 against current default factory/bootstrap as pending human merge; this branch is stacked for planning only.
risks: Radio Browser is an external, community-maintained provider: outages, rate/latency behavior, mirror availability, catalog errors, and stale station records can affect discovery.

The provider API documents a very large default result limit; omitting an explicit cap risks oversized MCP results/UI payloads. A fixed small list without pagination can omit desired stations and should be described honestly.
Provider-supplied names, tags, logos, and URLs are untrusted. Unsafe schemes, malformed metadata, redirects, unsupported codecs, or dead streams may cause unsafe rendering or playback failures.

The fixed DIAL-001 CSP origin cannot cover an unbounded set of selected station hosts. Allowing arbitrary media hosts, changing resource declarations per selection, or proxying streams each has security, host-compatibility, and complexity tradeoffs.
Counting station plays as recommended by the provider sends a playback event/IP to that service and adds an external request that could fail independently of actual audio startup.

The work branch is stacked on DIAL-001 while PR #1 for the current factory/bootstrap remains unmerged. Integration may require rebasing/cherry-picking after that human decision; do not build against an assumed merged baseline.
